title: 16:8 Intermittent Fasting Macro Calculator | Hacé Cuentas
description: Calculate daily macros for 16:8 intermittent fasting: 30% protein, 30% fat, 40% carbs over 2 meals. Free, instant results.
intro: **16:8 intermittent fasting** — known in the research literature as **Time-Restricted Eating (TRE)** — compresses your daily food intake into an 8-hour eating window (most commonly 12-8pm for late-eaters or 10am-6pm for early-birds), with a 16-hour fast covering the rest. The protocol is a *schedule*, not a magic metabolic switch. The landmark **Lowe et al. JAMA Internal Medicine 2020 TREAT trial** randomized 116 adults to 16:8 TRE vs. a 3-meal control and found **no significant difference in weight loss** when calories weren't tracked — confirming what every evidence-based sports nutritionist already knew: **the caloric deficit drives fat loss, the eating window just helps you create one passively**. Where 16:8 gets technically tricky is **macro distribution**: you still need 0.7-1.0 g of protein per pound of bodyweight for muscle retention (Schoenfeld 2018 review on protein timing), and squeezing that into 2-3 meals within 8 hours requires deliberate planning — typically 40-50g protein per meal to hit the leucine threshold (~2.5-3g) needed to maximally trigger muscle protein synthesis. This calculator splits your daily target across two meals (40% / 60%) at a balanced 30P / 30F / 40C macro profile so you can hit protein, manage satiety, and still enjoy carbs at dinner.
keyTakeaway: 16:8 IF: **30% protein + 30% fat + 40% carbs**. 8-hour window, 2 meals (40/60). 2000 kcal = 800 + 1200.
useCases: Losing weight without tracking calories daily — the compressed window naturally cuts 200-400 kcal/day for most people.
Simplifying meal prep — 2 meals instead of 4-5 means less cooking, less cleanup, less decision fatigue.
Managing blood glucose and prediabetes — pushing the eating window earlier (8am-4pm) improves insulin sensitivity per Sutton 2018 Cell Metabolism.
Fitting nutrition around shift work or a late commute — skipping breakfast is often easier than skipping dinner socially.
Building a sustainable lifestyle rather than another 12-week cut — TRE has high adherence rates because the rules are simple.

example.title: Example: 2000 kcal, 12 PM–8 PM window
steps: **Fasting**: 8 PM to 12 PM next day (16 hours).
example.result: Daily totals: 150g protein + 67g fat + 200g carbs across 2 meals.

explanation:
## What 16:8 Time-Restricted Eating Actually Is

16:8 is a **Time-Restricted Eating (TRE)** protocol — a sub-category of intermittent fasting where you eat within an 8-hour window and fast for 16. It's not Alternate-Day Fasting (ADF, eating every other day, Varady U Illinois research) and it's not a 24-hour weekly fast. The mechanism isn't a metabolic shortcut: the **Lowe 2020 JAMA Internal Medicine TREAT trial** found that 16:8 alone — without caloric tracking — produced no statistically significant weight loss beyond a control group. The compressed window helps because most people *spontaneously* eat 200-400 fewer calories when given fewer hours to eat. **The deficit drives the loss. The window helps you stay in one.**

## Picking Your Eating Window

| Window | Profile | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 PM – 8 PM | Late-eater (most common) | Social dinners intact, easy to skip breakfast | Hardest if you train early AM |
| 10 AM – 6 PM | Early-bird (best for glucose) | Best insulin/circadian per Sutton 2018 | Awkward for evening social events |
| 2 PM – 10 PM | Night-shift worker | Fits non-traditional schedules | Late carbs may affect sleep |

## Pre-Workout Fasted Training

Training fasted is **not catabolic at a meaningful level** if you're an adult eating enough protein in your 8-hour window. **Tinsley et al. 2017** (PubMed PMC5435671) compared TRE vs. normal eating in resistance-trained men and found **no difference in lean mass gains** over 8 weeks. Glycogen will be lower for fasted morning lifters — if you're doing high-volume strength work or sprints, train at the **end** of your fast and break it immediately after with a protein-led meal. For lower-intensity work (steady-state cardio, mobility), fasted is fine. If you want a hedge, **5-10g of EAAs or whey** mid-workout technically breaks the fast but preserves the metabolic benefits.

## Breaking the Fast: Meal 1 Composition

The first meal sets the tone for the rest of the window. Aim for:
- **40-50g protein** — beef, eggs, Greek yogurt, whey — hits the leucine threshold (~2.5-3g) to fully trigger Muscle Protein Synthesis (MPS) per Schoenfeld 2018.
- **Complex carbs** — oats, rice, potatoes — refill glycogen without the crash a Pop-Tart would give you.
- **Moderate fat** — keep it under 25g if you train shortly after; fat slows gastric emptying and can leave you sluggish.

Avoid sugar bombs (donuts, sweetened cereal). A 16-hour fast leaves you insulin-sensitive — the glucose response to a refined-carb meal is sharper than after a normal breakfast.

## Closing the Window: Meal 2 Composition

Your final meal should set you up for a 16-hour fast without triggering 3am hunger. Build it around:
- **40-50g protein** for the second leucine pulse — chicken, fish, ground beef, cottage cheese.
- **Anti-inflammatory fats** — olive oil, avocado, nuts, fatty fish — slow digestion and improve satiety.
- **Fiber-rich vegetables** — leafy greens, broccoli, bell peppers — bulk up the plate, slow glucose response.

## 2 Meals vs. 3 Meals in the Window

**Schoenfeld 2018** (review of protein distribution) shows MPS plateaus at ~3 leucine pulses per day. Two meals at 50g protein each gets you 2 strong pulses; three meals at 35-40g each gets you 3. **For lean mass goals, 3 meals (e.g., 1pm / 4pm / 7:30pm) wins marginally.** For weight loss simplicity, 2 meals wins on adherence. Both work — pick the one you'll actually do for 12 weeks.

## Caffeine, Supplements, and What Breaks the Fast

- **Black coffee, plain tea, water, electrolytes** — do not break the fast. Caffeine is fine during the 16-hour window and may even potentiate fat oxidation.
- **Creatine** — 5g daily timing is irrelevant per ISSN position stand. Take it whenever.
- **BCAAs / EAAs** — technically break the fast (insulin spike from leucine). If you're chasing strict autophagy windows, save them for inside the eating window. If you just want fat loss, they're a rounding error.
- **Diet soda, gum, zero-cal sweeteners** — debated. Most evidence says they don't break a fast for weight-loss purposes, but they may stimulate cravings in some people.

## TRE vs. ADF vs. 24-Hour Fast

| Protocol | Eating Pattern | Best For |
|---|---|---|
| **16:8 TRE** | Daily 8-hour window | Sustainable lifestyle, beginners |
| **20:4 (Warrior)** | Daily 4-hour window | Aggressive deficit, advanced |
| **5:2** | Normal 5 days, 500 kcal 2 days | Flexible weekly structure |
| **ADF** | Alternate fast/feast days (Varady U Illinois) | Research-backed weight loss |
| **24h weekly fast** | One full day off food | Metabolic flexibility experiment |

## 16:8 for Women

Women with low body fat, high training volume, or already-low caloric intake should approach TRE cautiously. **Cienfuegos et al. 2020 Cell Metabolism** found TRE safe and effective in obese women, but in lean, athletic females, chronic undereating in a compressed window can disrupt menstrual cycles via low energy availability. **Practical rule:** if your period becomes irregular, your eating window is too restrictive or your calories too low — widen to 14:10 or eat more.

## Refeed and Social Flexibility

A wedding, a work dinner, a Sunday with family — extending the window to 10-12 hours occasionally **does not derail results**. TRE works on weekly averages. Be strict 5-6 days, flexible 1-2.

**Avoid 16:8 if:** history of disordered eating, pregnant or breastfeeding, Type 1 diabetes, on glucose-lowering medication without doctor sign-off, or under 18.

faq.q: Is 16:8 actually better than just counting calories?
faq.a: **No — they're the same once calories are equated.** The Lowe 2020 JAMA TREAT trial showed no significant weight loss difference between 16:8 and 3-meal eating when calories weren't tracked. 16:8 *helps* you eat less without thinking about it, which is why people lose weight — but the deficit is still doing the work. Pick the one you'll stick to.

faq.q: Will I lose muscle training fasted?
faq.a: **Not at a practical level.** Tinsley 2017 (PubMed) compared TRE vs. normal eating in resistance-trained men and found equivalent strength and lean mass gains over 8 weeks. If you're worried, sip 5-10g of EAAs mid-workout or train near the end of your fast so you can eat protein within 60 minutes after.

faq.q: Does black coffee break my fast?
faq.a: **No.** Black coffee, plain tea, and water do not raise insulin meaningfully or break a fast for weight-loss, glucose, or autophagy purposes. Skip the cream, sugar, and "bulletproof" butter additions if you want the fasted state preserved.

faq.q: Should I eat 2 or 3 meals in my 8-hour window?
faq.a: **2 meals for simplicity, 3 meals for slight muscle-building edge.** Schoenfeld's protein distribution research suggests Muscle Protein Synthesis plateaus around 3 leucine pulses per day. Two meals at 50g protein still works great for fat loss; three meals (e.g., 1pm / 4pm / 7:30pm) at 35-40g each may marginally help if you're chasing hypertrophy.

**Yes for most, but watch for menstrual changes.** Cienfuegos 2020 Cell Metabolism showed TRE was safe and effective in obese women. In lean, athletic females, undereating in a tight window can disrupt cycles via low energy availability. If your period becomes irregular, widen to 14:10 or raise calories — don't push through.

**Yes**, as long as you hit 0.7-1.0 g protein per pound of bodyweight daily (Schoenfeld 2018 review) and you're at maintenance or a small surplus. The challenge is volume: getting 180g of protein into 2 meals means ~90g per meal, which is a lot of food. Three meals or a protein shake make it easier.

faq.q: Should I skip dinner instead of breakfast?
faq.a: **Skipping breakfast is more popular, but skipping dinner (10am-6pm window) is metabolically slightly better.** Sutton 2018 Cell Metabolism showed early-restricted feeding improved insulin sensitivity and blood pressure more than late-eating windows. Pick the one that fits your social and training schedule — adherence matters more than 5% metabolic edge.

faq.q: Is creatine OK during the fasted window?
faq.a: **Yes — timing doesn't matter.** Per the International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) position stand on creatine, 3-5g daily produces the same muscle saturation regardless of when you take it. Pre-workout, post-workout, with a meal, in fasted state — all equivalent over time.

faq.q: How long until I see results on 16:8?
faq.a: **2-3 weeks for energy/mental clarity, 4-6 weeks for measurable weight loss.** Assuming you maintain a deficit. If you're not losing weight after 6 weeks, you're eating at maintenance — the window doesn't override calories.

faq.q: What if I'm hungry at the end of my fast?
faq.a: **Push fluids, caffeine, and salt.** Most hunger in the 14th-16th hour is dehydration plus caffeine withdrawal. Drink 16 oz of water with a pinch of salt and a black coffee. If true hunger persists past week 2, your eating window may be too low in calories or too low in protein — increase both meals before shortening the fast.
